In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new methodologies for joint inversion of satellite-detector magnetic signals and their application to the study of Earth's electrical conductivity structure and water content of Earth's upper mantle and transition region.
a novel methodology of deriving electrical conductivity models, which is based upon joint inversion of satellite-detided tidal and magnetosphering signals.
the development of a new methodology for deriving global electrical conductivity models of the Earth's mantle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model is compatible with the presence of a small amount of water in the upper mantle, but it is not compatible with the presence a large amount of water in Earth's transition zone.
the new model is consistent with the pyrolytic model of the upper mantle with a small admixture of water in the transition zone.
the upper mantle and the transition zone have a pyrolyte-like composition, which is consistent with the presence of water at the 0.1% level in both regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the upper mantle and the transition zone are dry and pyrolytic.
we were able to derive a model of Earth's electrical conductivity, which is consistent with both laboratory measurements and geodynamical models.
the new global conductivity model is consistent with a hydrous mantle and that the model can be further improved by including other data sets and more sophisticated inversions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
joint inversion of satellite magnetic signals of magnetospheric, tidal and crustal origin provides a new and powerful approach for constraining electrical conductivity of the deep Earth.

the new methodology can be applied to any satellite mission, which provides magnetic field data with high spatial and temporal resolution, and thus can be used to derive global conductivity models with unprecedented spatial resolution.
satellite magnetic data, when properly processed and interpreted, provide a unique tool for probing the electrical conductivity structure of the deep Earth.
